summary: Rode 71.7 miles from Springfield MO to Carthage MO after a flat tire and a road closure where the road segment was missing; a passing driver led them on a short detour. Hosts in Carthage gave them watermelon and a scenic route past the Battle of Carthage site.
slept_at: Travis and Abi's house, Carthage MO (host)
contacts: Travis and Abi, Carthage MO (hosts)
planning_notes: Missouri road closure outside Springfield: a road segment was missing entirely. A local driver offered a detour of only a few extra miles; the team had called the support car to shuttle riders otherwise.
Carry a portable tire pump on the bike, not in the support car. They had a flat and the pump was in the car, so the driver had to come fix it.

summary: Rode 60 miles from Carthage MO into Kansas, where Google Maps routed them onto several miles of treacherous gravel. Took a rest day at Lake Crawford in Farlington KS after finding a missing day in their route spreadsheet and fixing it.
slept_at: Lake Crawford lakefront cabin, Farlington KS (host Nathan)
contacts: Nathan, Farlington KS (host at Lake Crawford)
planning_notes: Google Maps routed them onto several miles of gravel between Missouri and Farlington KS and does not fully account for slower speed on gravel. Cross-check with Komoot, which factors in road surface.
Kansas roads follow a nearly perfect grid, so detouring around closed roads is easy, but each mile has an intersection sign to maintain.
Route 76 (Transamerica) stays are often off-route; those routes need extra care.
Lake Crawford has boats, fishing and a lakeside cafe with wifi, useful for a rest day and shopping.

summary: Rider Simone was hit by a deer on Highway 54 in Kansas while riding the protected shoulder with sun glare in her eyes, about 6 miles from a 100-mile goal. She was checked at the local hospital and the team stayed at a church in Eureka KS; she then rested a few days and got a new helmet and pants at REI.
slept_at: Church in Eureka KS (church host; a member drove the team to the hospital)
contacts: Tressie, member of the Eureka KS church hosting the team (drove to hospital)
Pastor of the Eureka KS church (host)
planning_notes: Highway 54 in Kansas: wide protected shoulder, but deer jump out of roadside ditches. Sun glare made the deer invisible until impact. Watch ditch lines, especially at low sun angles.
Greenwood County Community Hospital (Eureka KS area) treated the rider well; the rider recommends a CT scan there if a crash involves a head impact.
Helmet replacement after a crash cost about $100 (Bontrager WaveCel); budget for a new helmet if one is hit.

summary: Reached the halfway point of the 80-day trip. Rode 75 flat miles on US Route 76 (Transamerica) from Eureka KS to Newton KS, where Warm Showers hosts (a Mennonite family) fed them tacos with local corn. A team member walked to a grocery store for berries and black grape juice for the solar-cell workshop.
slept_at: Warm Showers host (Mennonite family), Newton KS
contacts: Warm Showers hosts, Newton KS (Mennonite family; host cat Tiger and dog Enzo)
planning_notes: Route 76 (Transamerica) through Kansas: a roughly 40-mile stretch after Cassoday has no services. Cassoday Cemetery was one of the only stops before it, so fill water earlier.
Kansas law requires drivers to leave 3 feet when passing cyclists.
Solar-cell workshop dye: raspberries, blackberries and black grape juice all worked as anthocyanin sources. Buy them at the Newton KS grocery store about 0.7 miles from the host house.
Google Maps called the Eureka-Newton route 'mostly flat'; the actual climb was 876 ft, nearly flat.

summary: Taught a learning festival at the Newton Public Library in Kansas. Workshops covered color and chromatography and circuits. Then the team drove to Wichita to fix the car window and pick up bikes from a bike shop, but came back without the part needed to finish the bike repair.
learning_festival: Newton Public Library, Newton KS. Kids (advertised for ages 12-18) with librarian Sharon. Sessions: color/chromatography (markers, bubbles) and circuits (breadboard basics, LEDs, resistors, buzzers, buttons, paper speaker demo). BBQ lunch provided by the library.
contacts: Sharon, librarian, Newton Public Library (Newton KS)
planning_notes: Newton Public Library drew a crowd before doors opened; the library's flyer targeted ages 12-18. Expect a line of kids at opening.
Breadboard basics take the most time in the circuits workshop. Give extra time to breadboard before LEDs and buzzers.
Wichita bike shop: bikes sat waiting on a part the shop did not have. Call ahead to confirm parts before dropping bikes off.
Passenger window of the rental car failed, so the team needed a dealership fix. See the following day's post for the dealership visit.

summary: Left Newton KS late after an early-morning Ford dealership visit for the car window. Rode about 92 miles to Great Bend KS on flat, tailwind-assisted roads past tofu bean and sunflower fields. A helmet crack found at lunch sent one rider to the car for the rest of the day.
slept_at: Hosts Adam and Cassie, Great Bend KS
contacts: Adam and Cassie, Great Bend KS (hosts; Adam is a former chef)
planning_notes: A free cold-water cooler for cyclists sat along the Kansas route (location not stated). It was appreciated by riders.
A front shifter was fixed by wedging an Allen key into the derailleur, but that is a temporary hack. Carry spare Allen keys and check that structural parts are on the bike before leaving.
Check helmets for cracks before rides. A crack was found at lunch on this day and the rider switched to the support car.

summary: Rode 87.6 miles into a strong headwind from Great Bend to Dodge City KS, past wind farms and grain elevators. The four riders drafted in a tight line about 5 feet apart, rotating the lead every 30 minutes. Dinner was pizza and local beer at the Dodge City Brewery with hosts Lindy and Warren.
slept_at: Hosts Lindy and Warren, Dodge City KS
contacts: Lindy and Warren, Dodge City KS (hosts)
planning_notes: Strong headwind on Kansas prairie: drafting in a tight group (about 5 ft apart) made the wind manageable. The leader pulls about 30 minutes, then drops to the back. It needs attention to spacing and braking.
Dodge City was a rough Wild West town, now a tame downtown with a pizzeria and brewery worth visiting.
Grain towers were useful distance markers on the flat route. They signal a gas station or town ahead.

summary: Rode 49.8 miles from Dodge City to Lakin KS with only three riders, shuttling the last 20 miles to a motel to avoid heat and wind. Host Lindy chased the team down to return four water bottles left behind. Lunch was El Salvadoran pupusas in Garden City KS.
slept_at: Motel in Lakin KS
contacts: Lindy, Dodge City KS (host; returned water bottles)
planning_notes: No place to refill water between Dodge City and the lunch stop in Garden City. Start with full bottles and carry extras in jersey pockets if you run out of cages.
Heat over 100 degrees by 1 pm in western Kansas. Leave as early as possible and plan to finish by early afternoon.
Garden City KS has a large Latin American community. An El Salvadoran food truck there served pupusas and horchata.
Team bedtime was about 8 pm with everything packed the night before for a 6 am start.

summary: Rode 85 miles from Lakin KS into Colorado, crossing a time zone change, in heat near 102 degrees and a headwind. Dinner was rotisserie chicken and General Tso's chicken at the motel.
planning_notes: Heat near 102 degrees on the Kansas-Colorado plains: leave before dawn to ride in the cooler hours.
Cattle trucks along the route produce a strong manure smell. Grasshoppers jump up as bikes approach in the fields (common in summer).

summary: Taught the 8th learning festival at Lamar Public Library in Colorado to a small group of four very engaged kids. The next day rode 81.5 miles from Lamar to Fowler CO, with a Dairy Queen stop at mile 36 when the gas station was closed.
slept_at: Warm Showers host, Fowler CO (not named in this post; the next post describes a Warm Showers host's table in Fowler)
learning_festival: Lamar Public Library, Lamar CO, 8th learning festival. Four kids. Activities: physics of sound and Spectrogram (Fourier transform), paper speaker in circuits (taught by Mariela and Franklin), and berry-juice solar cells tested in sunlight (about 0.45 V).
contacts: Lamar Public Library staff (Lamar CO; learning festival host)
planning_notes: Lamar-Fowler: one long straight road for about 30 miles with few services. The gas station at about mile 36 was closed, so the Dairy Queen was the only stop; the receipt survey gives a free mini blizzard.
Lamar CO: Wash Spott car wash also serves ice cream and soda (locals' recommendation). The car wash high-pressure wand was also useful for cleaning bikes and the car.

Solar-cell testing: direct sunlight gave about 0.45 V, but multimeters were inconsistent. Wiring several cells in series did not light a red LED (needs about 2 V); check connections and sunlight first.
Workshop tip: change slides the night before to refresh the lesson.

summary: Rode from Fowler CO into Colorado's foothills; the plains turned to desert and then hills. A thunderstorm forced a car ride for the last part into Colorado Springs. The team met a solo touring cyclist named Caleb and learned Vail Pass (10,662 ft) is ahead.
slept_at: Host Ken, Colorado Springs CO (named in the next post; not named here)
contacts: Ken, Colorado Springs CO (host)
Caleb, solo touring cyclist (Chicago loop)
planning_notes: Thunderstorm forced a car ride for part of the day. Keep the sag vehicle available for storm bail-out.
Vail Pass (10,662 ft) is the Rockies crossing ahead for westbound riders on this route. Plan for it.

summary: Rest day in Colorado Springs with a 23-mile morning ride to Garden of the Gods with host Ken. Met the Stanford Spokes team at a Subway in Ellicott CO and got bikes repaired at Ted's Bicycles in Colorado Springs. On July 20 rode 65 miles on the 105 country road to Centennial, CO, with lunch at O'Brien's Cafe in Sedalia.
slept_at: Renee and Brad, Colorado Springs (night of July 19); Esther and Steve, Centennial CO (night of July 20)
contacts: Ken, Colorado Springs (host)
Renee and Brad, Colorado Springs (hosts)
Ted's Bicycles, Colorado Springs (bike shop)
Esther and Steve, Centennial CO (hosts)
Frances and Edmarie, Centennial CO
Thomas, Sedalia CO (paid for lunch at O'Brien's Cafe)
planning_notes: Ted's Bicycles in Colorado Springs: new wheel and shifters on two bikes, described as a fantastic shop.
Colorado Springs area has heavy weekday cycling and running traffic, so bike paths are busy.
The 105 country road from Colorado Springs toward Boulder is scenic and mostly downhill, but the route includes some climbing near Boulder.
Ellicott CO Subway: a good meetup point with other touring teams passing through.

summary: July 21 was a split rest day in Denver. The team replaced a defective rental car window while a friend and the author toured Red Rocks, Lookout Mountain and Meow Wolf. On July 22 the team rode 54 miles from Centennial to Blackhawk CO, climbing 5,353 ft into the mountains, and got a triple rainbow on the way.
slept_at: Hosts Amanda and Mike, Blackhawk CO (mountain home)
contacts: Amanda and Mike, Blackhawk CO (hosts)
planning_notes: Rental car problems in Denver: a defective window, then a trunk that would not stay open with the bike rack. The team swapped cars twice; ask the rental company about bike-rack compatibility first.
Denver bike paths: cyclists must yield to pedestrians and horses. Riding through Denver felt like Boston.
Lookout Mountain (Golden CO) is popular with road cyclists and has a climb to the lookout.

summary: Rode 55 miles from Blackhawk to Silverthorne CO and climbed 7,055 ft, including Loveland Pass near 12,000 ft. Cold rain and hail left riders without enough warm layers, and the support car picked them up. A steep gravel descent into Idaho Springs wore out hands and brakes.
slept_at: Host Stephen's home, Silverthorne CO
contacts: Stephen, Silverthorne CO (host; picked riders up at Loveland Pass)
Stephen's neighbors and friends (dinner)
planning_notes: Loveland Pass (near 12,000 ft): cold rain and hail even in July. Carry warm layers, not just summer kit, and plan a bail-out option.
Gravel descent into Idaho Springs (about a -6% grade): hands take a beating from the shocks and brakes. Take breaks to cool disc brakes.
Afternoon thunderstorms in the Rockies are near daily. Carry cards or something to do while waiting out storms.
Bears near the Blackhawk area: keep food indoors and do not leave food in cars. Bears open car doors to get food.

summary: Rode 90.7 miles from Silverthorne CO to Glenwood Springs, mostly downhill out of the Rockies, including a descent from Vail Pass through Vail. Stayed with Warm Showers host Greg in Glenwood Springs, who performed a card-magic show that evening.
slept_at: Warm Showers host Greg, Glenwood Springs CO
contacts: Greg, Glenwood Springs CO (Warm Showers host; magic show)
planning_notes: Vail Pass descent is long and fast. Stop to let brakes cool.
Google Maps routed the team through Vail's main street, which had a farmers market. Check the route manually on market days.
Hosts warned about mudslides on hillsides after wildfires, when a heavy rain can move soil onto roads below.

summary: Rode about 9 miles of I-70 shoulder between Glenwood Springs and Rifle CO on purpose. The interstate option (27 miles, 250 ft gain) was preferred over the other route (47 miles, 4,000 ft gain, about 6 hours). The shoulder was wide with a rumble strip, and drivers moved over for the team's high-visibility vests.
contacts: Tom Cravens, Hazard and Liberty KY (past host for learning festival and housing; referenced)
planning_notes: I-70 shoulder between Glenwood Springs and Rifle CO: a large shoulder with a rumble strip. Drivers moved lanes for bright yellow and pink high-visibility vests.
Interstate option (27 miles, 250 ft gain, about 2 hours) saved about 3,750 ft of climbing versus the non-interstate route (47 miles, about 6 hours). Compare Google's route options for mountain areas.

summary: Sophia took a rest day after 5 hours of sleep. The bikers rode from Rifle CO to a lunch stop in De Beque, where a police activity and a storm interrupted; the support crew shuttled the bikers past an interstate section because it was unsafe after rain. The team ended in Grand Junction CO with host Erika, who made a spaghetti dinner.
slept_at: Host Erika's house, Grand Junction CO
contacts: Erika, Grand Junction CO (host)
planning_notes: Western Colorado afternoon thunderstorms: plan the lunch stop for shelter. The De Beque town park gazebo has a holed roof but was usable.
Part of the route between Rifle and Grand Junction is I-70. The shoulder was not safe after rain, so the support car shuttled riders.
Police asked the team to stay in the De Beque gazebo while a fugitive was at large nearby. Check local news on route days.
Team discussed night rides starting 3 to 4 am for the Utah desert, but had not decided.

summary: Rode 84.6 miles from Grand Junction through Fruita on separated bike paths, then into desert on gravel after the Utah line. Stopped in Cisco UT, a ghost town with an artist community. Camped at Thompson Springs RV Park, where teammates cooked a chicken taco dinner.
slept_at: Thompson Springs RV Park, UT (camping)
planning_notes: Grand Junction to Fruita has nice separated bike paths. The team's hand-annotated map called Fruita 'the end of civilization', so stock up at the Sinclair gas station there.
The desert between Fruita and Thompson Springs has no shade and few trees. Water breaks in what shade exists were needed.
After the Utah border the road turns to loose gravel and slows riding, especially with a headwind.
Utah border sign: a spray-painted piece of plywood, not an official sign (not important for planning).

summary: After a rainstorm the team started late and rode 50 miles from Thompson Springs UT to Moab. They stopped at Jackass Joe's Jerky for gas station water and ice cream, rode through Arches National Park, and stayed at the Lazy Lizard Hostel in Moab.
slept_at: Lazy Lizard Hostel, Moab UT
contacts: Lazy Lizard Hostel, Moab UT (lodging)
planning_notes: Jackass Joe's Jerky (on the Thompson Springs-Moab route): gas station water and ice cream stop.
Arches National Park can be ridden through on the route to Moab; many photo stops.

summary: Left Moab on a bike path, then hit one of the worst shoulders of the trip, with trucks, RVs and cars passing every minute. The team called Robert to shuttle them to the end of that road. The rest of the 52-mile day was smooth and they camped at Green River State Park.
slept_at: Green River State Park campsite, UT
planning_notes: Road out of Moab: the shoulder was too narrow for bikes, with heavy traffic. The team shuttled the worst stretch.
The bike path out of Moab is pleasant, but it ends at the bad road. Plan for a shuttle or an alternative route there.

summary: A hard day: the team left late and was routed onto a sandy, almost non-existent road, then rode in the dark with no phone service and weak front lights. Support car Dora and Simone found them about 10 miles from the campsite. They camped near Capitol Reef with no showers, and a cyclist named James suggested stopping at Mesa Farm Market.
slept_at: Campsite near Capitol Reef NP (no showers)
contacts: James, cross-country cyclist (route tip: Mesa Farm Market)
planning_notes: Avoid the sandy unpaved road out of Green River State Park toward Capitol Reef. Tires sank in sand, and one section ran into a riverbed. It was the worst path of the trip.
Mesa Farm Market is one of the only points of civilization on the route to Capitol Reef. Stock up there.
No cell service on this stretch. A rider could not reach the support car; the team debated a satellite phone.
Charge all front and rear lights before a day that may run late. The team pedaled in pitch dark with weak phone lights.
A gas station along the route (location not stated) was carved into a rock and sold fruit ice-pop bars.

summary: Rode 49 miles from Escalante to Bryce Canyon NP on Scenic Byway 12, with trees growing from rock crevices and red, yellow and pink rock cliffs. A thunderstorm caught them; they sheltered at a trailhead bathroom until the support car came. The team also attended a rodeo that evening.
slept_at: Bryce Canyon area campground (named in the next post as Bryce Canyon Pines Campground)
planning_notes: Scenic Byway 12 (Escalante to Bryce): winding and nearly car-free, with many scenic turnouts. The team biked past them rather than stopping, but turnouts are good for photos.
Afternoon thunderstorms in Utah can come quickly. A trailhead bathroom gave shelter. The post suggests counting seconds between lightning and thunder and dividing by 5 for miles.
Rodeo events near Bryce include mutton busting, a kids' sheep-riding event.

summary: Rest day in the Bryce Canyon area for Maxwell's 23rd birthday. The team had breakfast pies, mountain biked (dropped at the wrong trailhead, then a riverbed detour), toured hoodoos in Bryce Canyon NP, ate a buffet dinner and gave Maxwell a handwritten card.
slept_at: Bryce Canyon area campground (not named in this post)
planning_notes: Mountain biking near Bryce: confirm the trailhead before setting out. The team was dropped at the wrong one and biked a riverbed for half an hour.
A buffet in the Bryce area opened later in the day; plan rest day meals around buffet hours.

summary: Rode 74 miles from Bryce Canyon Pines Campground to Cedar City UT past hoodoos, slot canyons, sheep and the Zion Overlook. An unpassable grass road and an ATV trail cost time, and a small cave crawl was part of lunch. The team stayed with Warm Showers hosts Pat and Ken, who hosted a pizza party. The support car got a flat tire that day.
slept_at: Warm Showers hosts Pat and Ken, Cedar City UT
contacts: Pat and Ken, Cedar City UT (Warm Showers hosts; pizza party; support-vehicle drivers for cross-country riders)
planning_notes: Komoot routed the team onto a road that turned into waist-high grass and was impassable. They turned back. Check satellite imagery for road surface.
Google Maps routed riders onto an ATV trail near Duck Creek Village, with bumps, mud and 45-degree pushes. Avoid ATV trails near Duck Creek Village.
The Ashdown Gorge descent after the Zion Overlook is long and fast (over 40 mph); it is cold with wind chill, so plan layers.
Navajo Lake overlook: good photo stop on the climb. Sheepdogs (5 dogs) came at the team near a sheep herd; the team formed a barricade with bikes until the dogs calmed.

summary: The support car had a flat tire on the descent from Bryce; the team swapped in the spare, then replaced all four tires in Cedar City. Robert tested positive for COVID and was sent to isolate in a Reno hotel, driven across Nevada by Mariela and Amira. Riders slept at Mountain View Baptist Church in Milford UT.
slept_at: Mountain View Baptist Church, Milford UT (church host)
contacts: Ken and Pat, Cedar City UT (hosts; flexible with the rental car)
Sandi, MIT travel coordinator (helped decide on tire replacement)
Amira (friend who helped escort Robert to Reno)
Mountain View Baptist Church, Milford UT (church host)
planning_notes: Cedar City UT has a tire shop with all-wheel-drive tires in stock, and a population of about 33,000. The nearest large rental-car center is in Las Vegas, about 2.5 hours away each way.
Budget rental: the team paid for four new tires up front and hoped for reimbursement. Ask the rental company before paying for repairs.
Stock up in Cedar City: it has the last Starbucks and the last supermarket with fresh produce until Fallon NV, about eight days later.
US 50 across Nevada ('the Loneliest Road in the US') has long gaps with no services. Do not drive it on a spare tire.
Plan a COVID contingency: a positive test meant a 9-day separation with a hotel isolation in Reno NV.
